thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike detected - llama-3a family TPM > expected baseline (x6) across us-east-1 pools. Auto-sculpt triggered -> applying soft caps if rate not reduced in 2m. Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/internal/d/llama3a/tpm
Maya (oncall): seeing 500-600 tpm sustained on llama-3a-prod, latency p50 climbing 120ms -> 300ms on plated pods. Customers with long-running chats might see stalls.
Rachel (eng-sre): confirmed. Error rate low but queues growing. Kernel-level metrics show KV cache pressure.
Tom (eng-runtime): is this coming from a single API key or broad?
Jen (support): support queue has 3 tickets complaining about timeouts; all from different customers.
Maya (oncall): quick breakdown from logs: ~70% requests from a new app in beta (key: xxx-****), but others also increasing.
Sam (eng-platform): I can append a per-model soft throttle rule to reduce sustained TPM for llama-3a to 200 TPM and RPM to 400, 60s window. Should we do that now as a temporary mitigation?
Maya (oncall): yes, do it. We want to avoid full disable. Post the exact command here so I can ack and monitor.
Tom (eng-runtime): command to add sculpt rule (console):
```
POST /api/v1/traffic/shape
{
  "model_family": "llama-3a",
  "scope": "us-east-1",
  "type": "per_model",
  "tpm_limit": 200,
  "rpm_limit": 400,
  "window_seconds": 60,
  "mode": "soft"
}
```
Sam (eng-platform): running now from the control plane. deploy-bot will confirm.
deploy-bot: executed traffic-shape job id=ts-2034567890-01 by Sam. Applying rule to us-east-1 -> target pools: rpool-a, rpool-b.
Maya (oncall): seeing immediate drop in accepted tpm to ~210, backlog clearing. Latency P50 falling. Thanks.
Rachel (eng-sre): note: soft mode will respond with 429s with Retry-After for excess requests. We should add a header-based hint for SDKs. Tom, can runtime attach `X-RateLimit-Note: transient-sculpt`?
Tom (eng-runtime): yes, I'll add that header for the sculpt window. Implemented in prod path; next requests include header.
Jen (support): I'll update support triage template: explain transient per-model throttling, guidance to exponential backoff.
Lucas (cust-success): flagging top 5 enterprise customers to be proactive via email/CS: possible latency spikes; no data plane degradation expected beyond transient 429s.
Maya (oncall): I'm going to raise RPM cap on a small traffic bucket for one partner (partner-B) that was impacted earlier. Command: `PATCH /api/v1/quota/partner-B` set llama-3a tpm=400 rpm=800 for 30m. Approving?
Sam (eng-platform): approved. Making exception for partner-B (client-id pb-002).
deploy-bot: quota patch applied for pb-002 -> ttl=1800s.
Maya (oncall): also enabling temporary stream-disable flag for llama-3a on best-effort tier to reduce long-lived streams. This should reduce KV cache pressure. Will revert in 1h.
Tom (eng-runtime): stream-disable toggled. Note: client connections will get a hint to fall back to chunked polling. We'll monitor errors from SDKs.
Rachel (eng-sre): Observability notes: created a dashboard panel and a /perf incident note. Added alert if tpm > 250 for more than 5m after sculpt removal.
Maya (oncall): timeline and impact: 2034567890 apply sculpt -> 2034567925 sculpt effective -> 2034567990 partner-B exception -> 2034568050 stream-disable -> current. Impact: transient 429s to best-effort tier, partner-B unaffected for 30m.
Jen (support): copying canned message for customers: "We're seeing elevated usage on a model family; we've applied temporary per-model shaping to preserve overall platform availability. You may see brief 429s; we recommend exponential backoff. Contact support if you see persistent failures."
Lucas (cust-success): I'll send heads-up to enterprise list with mitigation details + ETA for rollback (T+60m).
Maya (oncall): OK team. If metrics remain healthy at T+30m we remove sculpt and lift stream-disable. If tpm reverts to >250 we escalate to emergency throttle strategy (partial model disable across best-effort pools).
Rachel (eng-sre): leaving runbook tasks: 1) Check KV hit-rate and eviction counters; 2) Confirm no eviction storms; 3) Confirm autoscaler didn't spin extra cold nodes.
Tom (eng-runtime): runtime note: we observed increased KV cache churn from large context windows. Suggest follow-up: recommend quantization profile for llama-3a to reduce memory pressure.
Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm on for next 45m; if I get paged please follow this thread. @Rachel you'll take over if I need to escalate.
Rachel (eng-sre): ack. We'll keep monitoring.
Maya (oncall): closing loop here in ~60m with postmortem if we had any customer-impacting timeouts. For now marking status: MITIGATED (soft sculpt + partner exception + stream-disable).
